# A Few Notes on Integrals

To begin with, the following is the simplest way to integrate:

$$\int_a^bf'(x)dx=[f(x)]_a^b=f(b)-f(a).$$
In most cases in this module, integrals will be either of this form or some other
known integrals.

Also, a table of common antiderivatives is shared below for your convenience:

| $f(x)$ | Antiderivative of $f(x)$ |
|:---|:---|
| $1$ | $x$ |
| $x$ | $\dfrac{x^2}{2}$ |
| $x^2$ | $\dfrac{x^3}{3}$ |
| $x^n$ | $\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}$ |
| $e^x$ | $e^x$ |
| $\sin x$ | $-\cos x$ |
| $\cos x$ | $\sin x$ |
| $\dfrac{1}{x}$ | $\ln x$ |

Also, a nice property of integrals is linearity, i.e., that:

$$\begin{aligned}
  \int_a^b cf(x)dx&=c\int_a^bf(x)dx.\\
  \int_a^b f(x)+g(x)x&=\int_a^bf(x)dx+\int_a^bg(x)dx.
\end{aligned}$$
